verdict.rationale: First-party docs describe a dedicated headless mode. It runs a single task with `--prompt`/`-p` and exits, and accepts piped stdin. It emits a final JSON object and uses timeout exit codes. It offers an approval policy (auto/deny), and `runMC` is explicitly safe to embed in CI scripts and servers. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of CI usage.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Pass `--prompt` (or `-p`) to run a single task and exit:
`runMC` never calls `process.exit` and never writes to global streams, so it is safe to embed in CI scripts and servers.
A single final JSON object (text, usage, tool calls/results, threadId, status)
Exit with code 2 if not complete within the timeout
`auto` (default) approves everything; `deny` refuses approvals and aborts on suspension
